items.title: The Dream Replay
items.question: Dream researchers find dreams mostly continue waking preoccupations — students dream exams, soldiers dream patrols. What do dreams replay?
items.correctExplanation: Waking concerns — continuity hypothesis: dreams process daytime residues, not symbols from elsewhere. Days echo nightly.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is waking concerns. Static, prophecy, and pure repression miss it: content analyses tie dreams to daily life reliably. Nights continue days, rarely invent them.
items.lessonContent:
Nights continue days reliably here.
Content ties to daily life.
Residues replay; symbols rarely visit.
Continuity beats mystery in dreams.
Share this: log one day-residue dream.

items.title: The Spindle Predictor
items.question: Overnight improvement at motor skills tracks one specific sleep feature: brief bursts of sigma-band brain activity. What predicts the gain?
items.correctExplanation: Sleep spindles — stage-2 bursts whose density forecasts motor consolidation. Spindles stitch skills overnight.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is sleep spindles. Vividness, snores, and pillows miss it: sigma bursts mark offline replay that cements procedures. Density predicts improvement precisely.
items.lessonContent:
Bursts mark offline replay nightly.
Density forecasts improvement precisely.
Spindles stitch skills while bodies rest.
Sigma predicts motor gains well.
Share this: protect one spindle-rich night.

items.title: The Tired Confabulator
items.question: Sleep-deprived volunteers don't just remember less — they confidently 'remember' things that never happened. What does sleep loss inflate?
items.correctExplanation: False memories — tired brains confabulate: suggestibility rises as monitoring falls. Loss plus invention defines sleepy recall.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is false memories. Honest forgetting would be kinder: deprivation manufactures confident fictions. Monitoring fails before storage does.
items.lessonContent:
Monitoring fails before storage does.
Tired brains confabulate confidently.
Fictions fill gaps fatigue opens.
Loss plus invention defines recall.
Share this: distrust one tired memory.

items.title: The Heavy Nap
items.question: Twenty-minute naps refresh, but two-hour naps wake groggy and impaired. What punishes long naps?
items.correctExplanation: Sleep inertia — waking mid-deep-sleep drags grogginess for half an hour. Short naps dodge the deep end.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is sleep inertia. Dreams, alarms, and necks miss it: slow-wave awakening impairs transiently. Nap short or cycle-complete, never mid-depth.
items.lessonContent:
Mid-depth awakenings impair transiently.
Short naps dodge deep ends.
Inertia taxes long naps reliably.
Complete cycles or brief dozes.
Share this: cap one nap at twenty.

items.title: The Coffee Nap
items.question: Drinking coffee then napping twenty minutes beats either alone for alertness. What makes the combo best?
items.correctExplanation: Coffee naps — caffeine kicks in as the nap ends: adenosine cleared by sleep, receptors blocked by drug. Timing stacks benefits.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is coffee naps. Placebos, alarms, and rooms miss it: Hayashi's combo times pharmacology to awakening. Sleep clears, caffeine blocks, alertness doubles.
items.lessonContent:
Timing stacks drug plus nap benefits.
Caffeine kicks as naps end precisely.
Clearance plus blockade doubles alertness.
Combos beat solo interventions.
Share this: try one coffee nap.

items.title: The Drunk Tired
items.question: Staying awake 24 hours straight impairs driving roughly like what blood-alcohol level?
items.correctExplanation: Point-one percent — Williamson: a day awake ≈ 0.10% BAC territory, past legal driving limits. Tired steering equals drunk steering.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is point-one percent. Sober-feeling drivers perform drunk: vigilance, reaction, and judgment match intoxication. Wakefulness is no sobriety.
items.lessonContent:
Wakefulness is no sobriety ever.
Tired steering equals drunk steering.
Vigilance fails before eyelids do.
Drowsy drivers match drunk ones.
Share this: sleep before one drive.

items.title: The Next-Day Sponge
items.question: Pulling an all-nighter before learning destroys next-day uptake far more than it erases old knowledge. What does sleep loss hit hardest?
items.correctExplanation: New learning — Yoo showed encoding collapses without sleep while old memories persist. Sponges dry before libraries burn.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is new learning. Childhood, reflexes, and blinks miss it: sleep-deprived hippocampi can't file anything new. Encoding needs rest; retrieval coasts longer.
items.lessonContent:
Encoding needs rest; retrieval coasts.
Sponges dry before libraries burn.
New filing fails first nightly.
Sleep before learning, never after only.
Share this: sleep before one study day.

items.title: The Dream Journal
items.question: What reliably improves dream recall within weeks, with no supplements or devices?
items.correctExplanation: Dream journals — recording on waking trains recall rapidly: attention rewards remembering. Intention captures dreams.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is dream journals. Cheese, music, and lights miss it: morning logging signals the brain to retain. Recall is a practiced skill, not a gift.
items.lessonContent:
Logging signals brains to retain.
Intention captures fleeting dreams.
Recall practices like muscles do.
Mornings harvest night's work.
Share this: journal one dream tomorrow.

items.title: The Lucid Habit
items.question: What daytime habit most reliably induces lucid dreams at night?
items.correctExplanation: Reality testing — LaBerge: habitual day-checks ('am I dreaming?') spill into dreams, triggering lucidity. Day habits haunt nights.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is reality testing. Pills, alarms, and spice miss it: critical-state training transfers to sleep. Checks practiced waking fire dreaming.
items.lessonContent:
Day habits haunt nights reliably.
Checks practiced waking fire dreaming.
Critical states transfer to sleep.
Habits cross consciousness borders.
Share this: test reality five times.

items.title: The Rewritten Nightmare
items.question: What effectively rewrites chronic nightmares into milder dreams?
items.correctExplanation: Rehearsed endings — imagery rehearsal therapy: rescripting nightmares awake rewrites them asleep. Authorship cures horror.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is rehearsed endings. Pillows, bedtimes, and lamps miss it: daytime rescripting edits nighttime scripts. Authors revise dreams deliberately.
items.lessonContent:
Authorship cures nighttime horror.
Rescripting edits sleeping scripts.
Daytime revisions rewrite nights.
Endings rehearsed replace terrors.
Share this: rescript one nightmare.

items.title: The Unrecorded Stroll
items.question: Why don't sleepwalkers remember their nighttime strolls?
items.correctExplanation: Absent encoding — sleepwalking runs on NREM autopilot without memory formation. Actions occur; records don't.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is absent encoding. Lies, damage, and training miss it: partial arousals move bodies while memory stays offline. Strolls happen unrecorded.
items.lessonContent:
Partial arousals move bodies blindly.
Memory stays offline during strolls.
Actions occur; records don't follow.
Autopilot navigates memory-free.
Share this: lock one sleepwalker safe.

items.title: The Waking Lock
items.question: Why can't sleep-paralysis sufferers move despite feeling fully awake?
items.correctExplanation: REM atonia intrusions — dream-paralysis persists seconds into waking: mind awake, body locked. Atonia overstays.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is REM atonia intrusions. Sugar, water, and fitness miss it: muscle lockdown bleeds past dreaming into waking. Locks release slowly, never instantly.
items.lessonContent:
Locks release slowly, never instantly.
Atonia overstays into waking hours.
Minds wake; muscles lag behind.
Bleed-through paralyzes transitions.
Share this: wait out one lock calmly.

items.title: The Falling Twitch
items.question: What are the sudden twitches that jerk people awake just as sleep arrives?
items.correctExplanation: Sleep starts — hypnic jerks: the dozing brain misreads muscle relaxation as falling and startles. False alarms at sleep onset.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is sleep starts. Seizures, hearts, and nerves miss it: normal sleep-onset misfires, not pathology. Relaxation mimics falling briefly.
items.lessonContent:
Relaxation mimics falling briefly.
False alarms guard sleep onsets.
Normal misfires, never pathology.
Dozing brains startle easily.
Share this: twitch into sleep peacefully.

items.title: The Blocked Word
items.question: What is the tip-of-the-tongue state — knowing a word without retrieving it?
items.correctExplanation: Blocked retrieval — partial activation without completion: feeling-of-knowing with the word stuck. Gates jammed, not empty.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is blocked retrieval. Amnesia, freeze, and vu miss it: fragments (first letter, syllables) prove near-success. Retrieval blocks; storage holds.
items.lessonContent:
Fragments prove near-success always.
Gates jammed, never empty inside.
Partial activation teases completion.
Stuck differs from lost entirely.
Share this: unblock one word gently.

items.title: The Missing Years
items.question: Why do adults keep essentially no memories from before age three?
items.correctExplanation: Infantile amnesia — immature hippocampi plus pre-language encoding leave early years unrecorded. Cameras arrive after the opening scenes.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is infantile amnesia. Trauma, school, and parenting miss it: developing brains lack recording gear for autobiography. Encoding matures years after birth.
items.lessonContent:
Recording gear matures years late.
Cameras arrive after opening scenes.
Autobiography needs language plus hippocampus.
Early years pass unrecorded mostly.
Share this: forgive one missing year.

items.title: The Bump Years
items.question: Life memories bunch heavily between ages 15 and 30. What explains the reminiscence bump?
items.correctExplanation: Reminiscence bump — identity formation concentrates memorable firsts: love, work, independence cluster in youth. Selves crystallize memorably.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is reminiscence bump. Cameras, reunions, and marketing miss it: firsts cluster where identity forms. Novel self-defining decades stick hardest.
items.lessonContent:
Firsts cluster where identity forms.
Novel decades stick hardest always.
Selves crystallize memorably in youth.
Bumps mark becoming, never aging.
Share this: revisit one bump year.

items.title: The Shuffled Deck
items.question: Why does shuffled, interleaved practice beat blocked repetition of one skill?
items.correctExplanation: Mixed practice — interleaving forces discrimination between problem types: Rohrer's retrievals strengthen flexibly. Variety trains judgment.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is mixed practice. Hours, ease, and pencils miss it: shuffling demands type-identification every trial. Blocked drills polish; mixed decks prepare.
items.lessonContent:
Shuffling demands identification every trial.
Variety trains judgment, never just skill.
Blocked drills polish; mixed prepare.
Discrimination grows through interleaving.
Share this: shuffle one practice deck.

items.title: The Why Habit
items.question: What does asking 'why' while studying boost?
items.correctExplanation: Elaborative encoding — why-questions weave facts into networks: connections multiply retrieval paths. Explanation builds memory.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is elaborative encoding. Speed, counts, and colors miss it: interrogation connects new facts to old knowledge. Networks outremember lists.
items.lessonContent:
Interrogation connects new to old.
Networks outremember lists reliably.
Explanation builds durable memory.
Why-questions weave retrieval paths.
Share this: why one fact today.

items.title: The Double Channel
items.question: Why do diagrams plus text beat text alone for learning?
items.correctExplanation: Dual channels — Paivio's dual coding: verbal plus visual traces double retrieval routes. Two codes beat one.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is dual channels. Beauty, cost, and hours miss it: pictures plus words encode twice. Redundant traces survive forgetting better.
items.lessonContent:
Redundant traces survive forgetting.
Pictures plus words encode doubly.
Two codes beat single channels.
Verbals pair with visuals best.
Share this: sketch one concept today.

items.title: The Self Quiz
items.question: Why does attempting answers beat rereading them?
items.correctExplanation: Self-generation — producing answers strengthens paths reading never travels. Effort encodes; eyes merely tour.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is self-generation. Exercise, speed, and comfort miss it: retrieval practice builds what review skims. Generated answers stick; read ones slide.
items.lessonContent:
Effort encodes; eyes merely tour.
Retrieval builds what review skims.
Generated answers stick firmly.
Attempt first, reread second always.
Share this: self-quiz one page.

items.title: The Useful Struggle
items.question: Why does harder studying produce stronger, longer-lasting memory?
items.correctExplanation: Productive difficulty — Bjork's desirable difficulties: effortful encoding endures. Struggle strengthens storage.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is productive difficulty. Hours, books, and coffee miss it: difficulty that succeeds builds durability. Easy encoding evaporates; effortful persists.
items.lessonContent:
Effortful encoding endures longest.
Struggle strengthens storage reliably.
Easy evaporates; difficult persists.
Desirable difficulties build durability.
Share this: struggle productively once.

items.title: The Same Waters
items.question: Why do divers recall better underwater where they learned?
items.correctExplanation: Matching contexts — Godden and Baddeley: environments cue memories encoded within them. Places hold recall keys.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is matching contexts. Pressure, suits, and fish miss it: context reinstates encoding conditions. Learn dry, recall dry; learn wet, recall wet.
items.lessonContent:
Environments cue encoded memories.
Places hold recall keys silently.
Context reinstates learning conditions.
Match waters to remember dives.
Share this: study where tested once.

items.title: The Inner Weather
items.question: Why is recall best in the same mood or bodily state as learning?
items.correctExplanation: State matching — internal contexts cue like external ones: moods reinstate encoding states. Weather within matters.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is state matching. Coincidence, magic, and placebo miss it: Eich's moods function as contexts. Learn glad, recall glad best.
items.lessonContent:
Moods function as contexts fully.
Internal weather cues memories.
States reinstate learning conditions.
Glad learns recall glad best.
Share this: match one inner state.

items.title: The Edge Advantage
items.question: Why do list first and last items stick best?
items.correctExplanation: Primacy-recency effects — beginnings rehearse most, endings linger freshest: middles fade between. Edges win memory.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is primacy-recency effects. Fonts, volume, and length miss it: rehearsal favors firsts, recency favors lasts. Middles vanish between advantages.
items.lessonContent:
Beginnings rehearse most fully.
Endings linger freshest longest.
Middles vanish between advantages.
Edges win all memory contests.
Share this: front-load one list.

items.title: The Deep Dive
items.question: Why does meaning-based study beat rote repetition?
items.correctExplanation: Deep processing — Craik and Lockhart: semantic elaboration outlasts shallow rehearsal. Meaning anchors memory.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is deep processing. Hours, notebooks, and markers miss it: depth of encoding predicts durability. Elaboration beats repetition systematically.
items.lessonContent:
Elaboration beats repetition systematically.
Meaning anchors memories deeply.
Depth predicts durability reliably.
Semantic beats shallow always.
Share this: dive deep once today.
